crime: At eight, {WITCH_NAME} pictured pushing her grandmother down the cellar stairs, then ran and hid. From then on, she tossed a coin for every choice.

In the prison, she spent every evening at the upper railing beside a girl who leaned out over the courtyard to catch whatever was thrown up to her. One evening a throw came high, and the girl asked her to hold her waistband so she could lean farther. Gripping the cloth, she saw it again: her own hands pushing at the girl's back. She let go and tossed her coin. Will I push her?
The prisoners in the courtyard saw her arm at the girl's back as the girl fell to her death. At trial she told the court, "I let go." The prisoners convicted her of pushing.

But as the coin fell, her Magic made it swerve. It clipped the rail and flew out over the courtyard, and the girl, who snatched at every throw, snatched after it and went over the railing. She grabbed at the girl's back, too late; that was the arm the prisoners saw. Down in the courtyard lay the coin, and its answer was no.
fields.epitaph: She asked the coin whether she would push her. She never asked whether the girl would fall if she let go.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Gave Her Hands to a Coin
execution: In the trial court, the execution stand raises a giant iron coin on its edge. Beside it she lies chained flat, arms spread. An iron hand flicks the coin into a spin. It wobbles lower and faster, rattling, until it comes down flat on top of her. Beyond its rim, her open hand goes still.

magic.name: The Honest Toss
magic.text: Any coin, die or lot she casts with a question lands on the answer that will prove right.
